messages.subject: mixture model with nonlinear function
parts:
Hello,
     I'm trying to formulate a model with brms that I think is beyond its syntax (but it's such a nice package that I hope I'm wrong!). The goal is that each observation [o] is distributed as a weighted combination of K normal distributions whose means are parameterized by a nonlinear formula.

y[o] ~ w[1] * normal(mu[1], 1) + w[1] * normal(mu[2], 1) + ... + w[K] * normal(mu[K], 1)
mu[i] ~ non-linear function
w[i] ~ dirichlet [or, as some other formula to make it a simplex]

So, it's is a mixture model, where each observation is a combination of multiple components (I think this is a kind of latent dirichlet allocation model). I'm interested in estimating the parameters of the non-linear function, as well as the weights associated with each component. When I try to look at the available priors with the following formula (setting K = 3, eq2 is the non-linear function, gamma_tested is part of the experimental design, and kappa + gamma are the parameters of interest ):

mix <- mixture(gaussian, nmix = 3)
bf( y ~ eq2(gamma, gamma_tested, kappa),  
                      kappa ~ contrast, gamma ~ 1,
                      family = mix, nl = TRUE)
get_prior(form, data=d)

I receive: "Error: Non-linear formulas are not yet allowed for this family." Seems pretty clear that the model that the code implies isn't yet supported. But I'm a little unsure about this kind of mixture and wondered whether there might be another way to specify it with brms

Thanks,
Patrick

messages.author: 6e3dd74b422c061b
messages.subject: Re: [brms-users] mixture model with nonlinear function
parts: It is indeed not yet support, but I think in brms 1.10 I cleared the way to get this running. I hope it will be part of brms 2.0, which should be released before end of this year.
